Adept

/uh-DEPT/ - rhymes with kept · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Adept means extremely skilled.

Long winters made Aunt Vera adept at mending nets, her shuttle moving faster than the eye could follow.

Worked Example

The station's traffic reporter is adept at reading the city: give her three camera feeds and a rainfall report, and she will tell you which bridge will jam eight minutes before it does, rerouting half the morning's drivers around a stall they never see.

Adept is the right word because adept means extremely skilled — not merely able to do the job, but so practiced that the hard parts look routine. Skilled says you clear the bar; adept says you clear it every time, without visible effort, usually after years of repetition.

How Adept Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

proficient

proficient: solidly capable — a rung below adept's mastery

practiced

practiced: skill explained by repetition, without saying how far it reached

Antonyms

incompetent

incompetent: unable to do the job at all

amateurish

amateurish: the rough edges showing

How Strong Is It? — capable → adept → masterly

capable vs. adept

capable vs. adept: Capable clears the bar — the job gets done correctly, and that is all the word promises.

masterly vs. adept

masterly vs. adept: Masterly goes further than adept — the adept sailor wins the regatta; a masterly one seems to teach the wind itself how the race should go.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — ad-

Prefix — ad-: to, toward

Root — -ept

Root — -ept: grasp, attain (Latin apisci)

Put it together

Put it together: Ad- (toward) + -ept (grasp, attain) = having attained — one who reached the skill and holds it. Latin adeptus described an alchemist who had 'attained' the art's secrets; English kept the sense of skill fully grasped, with the alchemy quietly dropped.

Use the root in a new word: aptitude

Use the root in a new word: aptitude: A camp counselor with an aptitude for knots takes to every new hitch on the first try — the same root, a natural grip on a skill.

Word Choice

neutral / appreciative

Adept is broad praise for practiced, high-level skill at an activity — adept at chess, at coding, at calming toddlers. When the skill lives in the hands specifically, this unit's deft is sharper; when it is cleverness in a tight spot, adroit; for the loud, demonstrated feats themselves, prowess.
